concerns.text: T006 (dataset.schema.yaml) and T007 (model_output.schema.yaml) are listed as foundational tasks but are marked unchecked. T012 (ingestion) and T014-T016 (features) consume the 'AlloyRecord' structure defined in T006. T022-T023 (train) consume 'ModelMetrics' from T007. A consumer (T012) cannot execute before its producer (T006) is complete. These schema definitions must precede any data processing tasks.

T024 (statistical significance t-test) is marked as depending on T024a (null model distribution), but T024a is marked unchecked. T024 explicitly states it 'MUST raise AssertionError' if the null model distribution is missing or invalid. The consumer (T024) is placed before the producer (T024a) is guaranteed to exist, violating the 'Producer before consumer' rule.

T030a (collinearity check) is marked unchecked, yet T030b (stability verification) and T031 (sensitivity analysis) depend on its output (the 'stability_test_model.pkl'). T031 also depends on T022 (original model). If T030a fails or is skipped, T030b and T031 lack the required input artifact. The dependency chain is broken by the unchecked status of the producer task.

T010 and T011 (tests for US1) are marked [X] (complete) but are listed before T012-T017 (implementation). While TDD is a valid strategy, the task list implies these tests are 'ready to run' before the code they test exists. The ordering should reflect that these tests are 'written' (code exists) but 'fail' until T012-T017 are implemented, or the status should reflect 'pending implementation' to avoid confusion about artifact availability.
